title: Mind2Act World: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Embodied Mind, Physical Action, and Mind-Action Composition in Robotic Manipulation
title_zh: Mind2Act World：诊断机器人操作中的具身认知、物理执行及其协同的基准
abstract_en: Embodied intelligence aims to let robots perform complex physical tasks with human-like adaptability and reliability, which requires three complementary capabilities: history-based cognitive reasoning, precise and timely physical execution, and the composition of reasoning and execution through environmental feedback. Yet existing benchmarks either evaluate reasoning and execution within the same tasks or assess them separately without their composition, so they reveal little about whether a failure comes from reasoning, execution, or their composition. We introduce Mind2Act World, a diagnostic benchmark of 30 simulated manipulation tasks from five real-world application domains. Each task has three difficulty levels and two scene settings (Clean and Random), yielding 180 configurations. The tasks form three views: Mind tests decisions based on past observations, Act tests precise and timely execution, and Mind2Act combines both in closed-loop tasks where action outcomes guide later decisions. Comparing the three views shows whether a system lacks a capability or fails to compose capabilities it already has. A diagnosis harness further attributes the failed episodes of three representative systems to Mind, Act, or their composition and summarizes each system in a profile card. Our evaluation of multimodal agents, vision-language-action models (VLAs), and world-action models (WAMs) shows that competence in a single view does not carry over to Mind2Act tasks. Even the strongest agent succeeds in 52.7% of Mind and 39.0% of Act episodes but in only 12.0% of Mind2Act episodes. The strongest agent retains task state but struggles with sustained contact, whereas end-to-end policies execute practiced motions but retain little task state. These findings point to composing reasoning and execution through environmental feedback as the main open problem.
abstract_zh: 机器人要灵活、可靠地完成复杂操作，不仅要根据历史观测做出判断，还要精准、及时地执行动作，并根据环境反馈调整后续决策。现有基准往往难以区分失败究竟源于推理、执行，还是两者未能有效协同。Mind2Act World 涵盖五个现实应用领域的 30 项仿真操作任务，每项任务设有三个难度等级以及 Clean 和 Random 两种场景设置，共 180 种配置。基准从三个维度进行评测：Mind 测试基于历史观测的决策，Act 测试动作执行的精度和时机，Mind2Act 则测试能否根据动作结果调整后续决策，形成闭环。作者对多模态智能体、视觉-语言-动作模型（VLAs）和世界-动作模型（WAMs）进行评测，并通过诊断框架对三个代表性系统的失败进行归因。结果表明，单项能力并不能直接转化为闭环任务中的表现：最强智能体在 Mind、Act 和 Mind2Act 上的成功率分别为 52.7%、39.0% 和 12.0%。该智能体能记住任务状态，却难以维持物理接触；端到端策略能执行训练过的动作，却难以保留任务状态。结果凸显了利用环境反馈协调推理与执行这一关键难题。
key_points_zh: 基准覆盖五个现实应用领域的 30 项仿真操作任务，结合三档难度和 Clean、Random 两种场景设置，共形成 180 种配置。
Mind 和 Act 分别测试基于历史观测的决策与精准及时的动作执行；Mind2Act 则要求系统利用动作结果指导后续决策。
诊断框架将失败归因于 Mind、Act 或两者的协同，并用能力画像卡总结三个代表性系统的失效模式。
最强智能体在 Mind 和 Act 上分别达到 52.7% 和 39.0% 的成功率，但在 Mind2Act 上仅为 12.0%；它能记住任务状态，却难以维持接触，而端到端策略能执行训练过的动作，却难以保留任务状态。
